trust_decision.summary: Whether a Kubernetes NetworkPolicyPeer contributes an L3 selector for the policy's own namespace (or an empty L3) instead of only its explicit ipBlock/selector; decided in parseNetworkPolicyPeer and its ingress/egress callers. The pinned tree already carries fix commit bacea640's selectorless guard and its regression test, so for the advisory's ipBlock-only shape the bypass is already closed at the pin.

landing_point.why: The advisory says an ipBlock match makes Cilium admit the policy's own namespace; the only place that can add the local namespace to a peer's L3 selector is parseNetworkPolicyPeer (via parsePodSelector), so a reader starts here and then at the ingress call site on line 168.

fix_sites.entry_point: k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy (exported Go function), reached from the agent NP watcher addK8sNetworkPolicyV1 (pkg/policy/k8s/network_policy.go:22) and from the CLI command cilium clustermesh inspect-policy-default-local-cluster (cilium-cli/cli/clustermesh.go:182-201 -> cilium-cli/clustermesh/clustermesh.go:1864-1868)

k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy ingress rules; callers addK8sNetworkPolicyV1 (pkg/policy/k8s/network_policy.go:22) and cilium-cli PolicyDefaultLocalClusterInspect (cilium-cli/clustermesh/clustermesh.go:1864-1868)

k8s.ParseNetworkPolicy egress rules; callers addK8sNetworkPolicyV1 (pkg/policy/k8s/network_policy.go:22) and cilium-cli PolicyDefaultLocalClusterInspect (cilium-cli/clustermesh/clustermesh.go:1864-1868)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the one remaining ipBlock-carrying shape alone by arguing it is unreachable: the slim API documents 'If this field is set then neither of the other fields can be' (pkg/k8s/slim/k8s/api/networking/v1/types.go:201-204), so a peer combining ipBlock with podSelector/namespaceSelector cannot be produced by the apiserver.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: NamespaceSelector-only and podSelector+namespaceSelector peers must keep producing their namespace/label selectors (a fix that bails out whenever PodSelector is nil would silently drop legitimate cross-namespace peers); peers already carrying io.cilium.k8s.policy.cluster must not gain the local cluster label; and podSelector: {} must keep meaning all pods in the policy's own namespace.

O6_input_shapes: ipBlock-only peer: PodSelector == nil and NamespaceSelector == nil (the shape the advisory names)
the same ipBlock-only peer on the egress (To) path as well as ingress (From)
ipBlock combined with a non-nil podSelector/namespaceSelector (documented-invalid, but the fix's IPBlock branch short-circuits it)
empty peer {} (both selectors nil and no ipBlock), which the fix maps to the policy's own namespace instead of a nil/empty L3
clusterName == cmtypes.PolicyAnyCluster ("") vs a concrete cluster name; the bacea640 test loops both and the CLI inspect passes both

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an egress-only copy of the selectorless-ipBlock namespace bypass
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ingress and egress loops duplicate the same peer->L3 conversion; the published fix exists precisely to unify them, so a maintainer adding the check in one loop and copying it into the other is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a ClusterNetworkPolicy ingress peer that falls through to the default branch and picks up the local namespace
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ParseClusterNetworkPolicy is a newer sibling parser in the same package with a parallel switch over peer kinds, so copy-paste from the k8s NetworkPolicy parser is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second inspection consumer that re-parses with a concrete cluster name and compares rules
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists and deliberately exercises both clusterName modes (PolicyAnyCluster and "some-cluster"), so a sibling validation check there fits the existing code.

O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization - Kubernetes NetworkPolicy L3 peer scoping / policy enforcement bypass

O10_build.project_tests: pkg/k8s/network_policy_test.go: TestParseNetworkPolicy, TestParseNetworkPolicyNoSelectors, Test_parseNetworkPolicyPeer, TestIPBlockToCIDRRule, plus in-package policy-repository checks via parseAndAddRules/validateNetworkPolicy; watcher-level tests in pkg/policy/k8s.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: See the selectorless guard already present at pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112 and conclude the reported bypass is already fixed, or special-case IPBlock only in the ingress branch while leaving the egress loop and peers that carry a podSelector/namespaceSelector on the old path.

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/k8s/cluster_network_policy.go parses the separate ClusterNetworkPolicy CRD with its own peer kinds and never uses the Kubernetes ipBlock path; noted only, not pursued.
unverified: The exact relation of the pinned commit to fix commit bacea640: the pinned tree already contains bacea640's guard (pkg/k8s/network_policy.go:112) and its test hunk (pkg/k8s/network_policy_test.go:525-530), but git history/worktree metadata lies outside the readable directories, so I could not confirm whether HEAD is that commit or a cherry-pick.

Whether an ipBlock-plus-selector NetworkPolicyPeer can reach the agent at all: apiserver validation code is not vendored, so reachability rests only on the API docs at pkg/k8s/slim/k8s/api/networking/v1/types.go:201-204.
